highlights.title: Kids turned the comment section of an NPR podcast into a group chat
highlights.summary: Middle schoolers, likely blocked from other apps and social networks, apparently turned the Spotify comment section under an episode of NPR's Wild Card into an impromptu group chat. In a new episode of This American Life, host Ira Glass digs into how the kids landed there and why.
body: Blocked from other social media, middle schoolers have had to get creative.

When Glass asked one of the kids why they picked this particular podcast, they said, “We just, like, looked for podcasts that didn’t have many comments.” Which, obviously, hurt Glass’s feelings a bit.

Initially, showrunner Dave Blanchard thought the comments were a particularly odd strain of bot. “It was just like gibberish,” he tells Glass in the episode. The posts were “clipped, weird, incoherent,” he said, and loaded with emoji and shorthand. So he deleted them. Then one of the accounts posted, “so it deleted my com.” So Blanchard shared screenshots of the comments in NPR’s Slack.

Producer Hannah Chin almost immediately recognized the behavior not as bots, but as kids. “I was a kid who used weird parts of the internet not as they were originally designed to talk to my friends,” they said. “I talked back and forth with my friends on Google Docs,” demonstrating just how resourceful kids can be when cut off from traditional social media.
points: Middle schoolers, likely blocked from other apps and social networks, apparently turned the Spotify comment section under an episode of NPR's Wild Card into an impromptu group chat.

It was an interactive virtual avatar of him, trained to answer common press questions about Synthesia, like what it does and how it works. The day before, I was on a panel where PR people asked me if I minded pitches that used AI-generated text. But Alexandru’s avatar was beyond that — this seemed to me the final boss of using AI in PR.

In September, Synthesia invited me to its new office space in New York. Originally based in the U.K., Synthesia is a hot digital avatar startup alongside others like D-ID, HeyGen, and Colossyan. It hit a $4 billion valuation earlier this year and said last year it had crossed $100 million in ARR.

highlights.title: Putellas' first WSL goal helps send London City second with Brighton win
highlights.summary: Alexia Putellas scored her first goal in English football, helping London City Lionesses to a 2-0 win against Brighton and sending them second in the WSL table.
body: London City Lionesses vs Brighton and Hove Albion Women. Barclays Women's Super League.

The biggest signing of the summer collected a rebounded save after Chiamaka Nnadozie initially stopped Kadidiatou Diani's strike. She then swerved a half-volley around her defender that beat the still-recovering goalkeeper.

It was the first real chance of a first half that lacked many, although Brighton almost equalised instantly. Emily Murphy's header curled onto the crossbar though and Keiko Seike - who was impressive defensively - could not sort her feet out to slot home the loose ball.

Lucia Corrales rounded off the victory late on, finishing a wonderful team break. Danielle van de Donk stole the ball away from Fran Kirby, releasing Delphine Cascarino, who in turn picked out the incoming run of Corrales on the left, who emphatically finished.

highlights.summary: Supercell has moved Mo.co back into beta development after admitting the monster-hunting game is not performing as well as hoped. The current version will remain in low maintenance while the team experiments with new ideas and works on what comes next.... [ MORE ]
body: Despite the company admitting last month that the title will need bigger changes to achieve mass appeal, Supercell said it believes in the game and has more ideas planned for future testing.
“We previously shared that mo.co isn’t performing as well as we had hoped, and it will need bigger changes to get where we want it to be," the company wrote in a post.
“With that in mind we’ve decided to move the game back to Beta. The current game will continue on low maintenance while we focus on experimenting, testing new ideas, and building what comes next."
The current game will not receive new weapons in upcoming seasons, while seasonal passes will lose their premium tracks and weapons.

highlights.title: YouTube and Meta Reverse Course, Will Accept ‘Musk’ Trailer Ad
highlights.summary: The Google unit says the ad was "temporarily restricted" while Meta calls it "an error." TikTok and X remain silent.
body: Following an outcry over potential suppression, YouTube and Meta are changing direction on an ad for an Elon Musk documentary.

Bleecker Street, the studio behind Alex Gibney’s upcoming Musk, will be allowed to buy an ad for the trailer on the platform after all, a YouTube spokesperson tells The Hollywood Reporter. The trailer “was temporarily restricted by our system. Following review, the ad has been cleared to run,” the company said, also posting the message to social media.

On Friday, THR reported that YouTube, along with Meta, TikTok and X had all refused to allow Bleecker Street to run a paid ad for the trailer, raising the specter of suppression on a documentary about the very subject. The trailer had been released Thursday ahead of the film’s Oct. 9 release.

A YouTube spokesperson said the ad should be appearing soon, though as of late Saturday morning Bleecker Street has not yet been informed of any change. The company had been appealing the initial ruling from YouTube.

highlights.title: Dolce & Gabbana mixes it up as pressure mounts for turnaround
highlights.summary: With Jennifer Lopez providing some star power, the Italian house’s Milan show came at a crucial time for the brand. Earlier this week Jennifer Lopez walked down the Vogue World catwalk in Milan wearing a black beaded A-line bustier dress from Dolce & Gabbana.
body: The reminder of Dolce & Gabbana ’s inimitable celebrity connection is no coincidence. In a turbulent luxury market, the brand has found itself trying to navigate a nearly £400m debt pile.
In August, the company, embroiled in controversy over the years, reached an agreement with its banks that gave it until March 2028 to settle its debt.
In exchange for the waiver, the brand must carry out a series of “extraordinary corporate transactions”, which reportedly include the sale of some of its properties.
It is one of the few fashion houses that remains independent. Gucci and Bottega Veneta are owned by the French conglomerate Kering while Fendi has been absorbed by LVMH.

highlights.title: MIT students gain a humanist lens on technical innovation in Tulsa, Oklahoma
highlights.summary: The PKG Center expands Code.Tulsa, an internship program that places MIT students with tribal nations and Tulsa nonprofits to develop AI and data science projects while gaining humanistic perspectives on technology's role in community development.
body: When MIT mechanical engineering student Daphne Wang arrived for her internship at the Muscogee Creek Nation Department of Health in Tulsa, Oklahoma last summer, she expected to be writing code. To her surprise, she found herself analyzing tribal history and the implications for technical innovation.

“I learned so much that I think should be required curriculum for every single person in this country,” says Wang. “I think tech for good is genuinely getting out into communities and learning about people who aren't you, creating worldly perspectives that you ultimately can take into everything else that you do.”

Wang and fellow intern Lucy Sun, who is majoring in artificial intelligence and decision making, spent the summer supporting the development of the Muscogee Nation's first Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) survey to capture maternal health data specific to Muscogee women. The project required completing literature reviews, analyzing datasets, and drafting survey questions, while considering issues of data sovereignty and governance structures specific to the Muscogee.

highlights.title: Maracana pitch still being worked on with NFL match just hours away
highlights.summary: Workers were still trimming the turf at Maracana Stadium on Saturday, less than 30 hours before the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens.
body: The Maracana's pitch has been a concern for almost two weeks due to its poor shape amid a long season in Brazilian football, with Rio clubs Flamengo and Fluminense playing there at least once a week.
Maracana workers were using mows and scissors big and small to perfect the turf for the game, in an effort expected to end just hours before kick-off.

On Friday, the executive director of the NFL Players Association said both the NFL and the players union have had experts monitoring the field conditions for Sunday's game. The union's experts are worried about loose turf leading to too much slipping.
Concerns are about the turf's traction and stability, which made the NFL reinforce its stitching. Earlier this week, field director Nick Pappas said he was confident players will have no trouble.

Although it's far from the kind of dynamic themes or wallpapers fans have begged Sony to bring back, the animated background does add some flavor for fans still hoping to see the series get a proper return in games.

Those who want to spice up their PS5 backgrounds need only to navigate to the Welcome Hub, select the Change Background button in the top corner of the screen, and then select The Last of Us background in the Games tab. It's nothing much, but we'll only have to wait a few more days to hear more about The Last of Us Day celebration.

In a separate post, Naughty Dog promised September 28 will bring even more reveals for the franchise. While it doesn't sound like something like The Last of Us Part 3 will be discussed, the team did promise to share a "partnership announcement, a very cool collaboration, digital surprises, and more." There will also be a No Return charity stream on Twitch.

highlights.summary: Despite being fired from the “Scream” franchise in 2023, Melissa Barrera has made it clear that her real issue is with Spyglass Media Group, not the films themselves. When asked if she’d ever return for a future “Scream” film during a recent JustWatch interview, the actress responded, “not with the…
body: Barrera’s comments pertain to the company’s claim that she was acting antisemitically when she shared social media posts criticizing Israel amid the war in Gaza. At the time, Spyglass had said that it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.”

Barrera continued, “Even with an apology, I wouldn’t go back to work with them. So, not that I’m holding my breath. I don’t think they have that ability. But if the franchise were ever to leave those hands and go into hands that I think honor Wes Craven’s legacy more, I think yeah.”

The “In the Heights” actress had starred in 2022’s “Scream” and that year’s “Scream VI” before she was ousted from the franchise. “Scream 7” was released earlier this year. Recently, she spoke about how “beautiful” she found the support around Macklemore to be following his removal from Ed Sheeran’s tour for his support of Palestine.

highlights.title: ‘Charming and disarming’ … how Meta’s technology-packed Muse harnesses the power of cuteness
highlights.summary: The tech giant has launched a cute ‘little guy’ that can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop. After the recent backlash against Meta’s so-called “pervert” smart glasses, this week Mark Zuckerberg launched a much cuter alternative: the Muse “charm” device.
body: With a screen that shows a cutesy little avatar, it has drawn comparisons with Tamagotchis. “We’ve packed a lot of technology into this little guy,” the Meta founder told the San Francisco audience.

The “little guy” could fit, like a Labubu, on to a keychain or bag. But unlike a Labubu, the interactive AI assistant will have significant capabilities, including the ability to have live conversations. It can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop.

According to Katie Seaborn, a Cambridge associate professor who has been researching cuteness – creating the science of cute voices within the context of computing – it’s cute because it “basically looks like a baby”.

For Joshua Paul Dale, professor at Chuo University in Tokyo and author of Irresistible: How Cuteness Wired our Brains and Conquered the World: “It’s really significant that along with the wearable charm, Meta also introduced a new pair of smart glasses with no camera. Everyone hates cameras in smart glasses. But if the camera is contained in a charm you wear around your neck, it shifts the agency. Suddenly, you’re not recording people. It’s just a cute little animated avatar looking out on the world.”

highlights.title: Minecraft Is Getting Its First New Dimension In Over 15 Years
highlights.summary: Announced today during Minecraft Live, Mojang is adding the first new dimension to the blocky sandbox game in more than a decade and a half. The Sift is an ethereal-looking fourth dimension that was first marketed for Minecraft Dungeons 2, and it's now been confirmed that it's coming to the base…
body: The Sift is a major new addition for Minecraft, marking the first new dimension since 2011's The End, where players go to fight the Ender Dragon in the end game. Speaking to GameSpot, Minecraft Dungeons 2 creative director Mans Olson explained that the team wanted to make sure that The Sift felt distinct from the Nether and The End rather than becoming another hostile environment.
"We wanted to make sure that it was different. That it doesn't feel like the ones that already exist in the game," he confirmed.

Unlike the Nether and The End, where the environments feel immediately hostile thanks to dangerous environmental hazards and angry mobs, the developers wanted it to feel like somewhere players could potentially live.
That doesn't mean that The Sift will necessarily always be completely safe. In Minecraft Dungeons 2, the dimension is under threat from the Illagers, leaving its ecosystem in danger.

highlights.title: Hayley Kiyoko Wants to Make a Lesbian ‘Pirates of the Caribbean’: ‘Keira Knightley, But Gay’
highlights.summary: Hayley Kiyoko wants to sail the same-sex-loving high seas. The musician, novelist and filmmaker says her dream project is a queer take on “Pirates of the Caribbean.” “I would love to do a lesbian pirate show or movie — Keira Knightley, but gay,” she said.
body: The 'Girls Like Girls' director and fellow queer filmmakers Angela Robinson, Adam Shankman and Wash Westmoreland reveal their dream projects.

She’s hoping to turn her second novel, “Where There’s Room for Us,” into a film as well. “It’s a period piece, which no one wants to pay for, but they will one day,” she said to cheers and applause from the audience.

Adam Shankman, whose directorial credits include “Hairspray,” “Rock of Ages,” “Stop! That! Train!” and the upcoming Arnold Schwarzenegger and Alan Ritchson holiday action comedy “The Man With the Bag,” said his dream project is a big-screen adaptation of “ Spring Awakening,” the Tony Award-winning coming-of-age rock musical set in late 19th-century Germany.

Although he doesn’t think it could ever get the go-ahead because of its intense subject matter, “where terrible things happen to these kids,” Shankman said, “I think it is such a beautiful poem and it is such a beautiful story and it lives in me in such a haunting and beautiful way. I know exactly what I would do with it, and I know exactly how I would do it. I see it completely, and I would love to make it more than any other movie. If that was my last movie, I’d be fine.”

highlights.title: Comedian Edy Modica Is Just Like You (But Funnier)
highlights.summary: It’s been a busy few years for Modica, who just released her first stand-up special, “I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks).”
body: When comedian Edy Modica arrives at the Condé Nast offices in downtown Manhattan, she looks as if she’s just wrapped filming on a Bravo show—her hoop earrings are sparkly and huge, her heeled denim boots coordinate perfectly with her long denim shorts, and a nameplate necklace spells out EDY. As I soon learn, that is, in fact, exactly the case; Modica is coming straight from guest-bartending on an episode of Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen.

Modica is promoting I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks), her chatty, confrontational, and sometimes crude debut special. (One of its best parts revolves around a young Modica browsing sites with names like “boobs.com” and “sex.com.”) But her strong and singular comedic voice has remained largely unchanged since I saw her perform a fully nude show at Williamsburg’s now-shuttered Annoyance Theatre a decade ago. I struggle with how to bring it up without sounding like a pervert, but Modica excitedly tells me that she remembers the set well; in fact, both of her parents were in attendance.

highlights.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
highlights.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models.
body: OpenAI keeps uncovering incidents of its models behaving in ‘unexpected or concerning’ ways.

In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. The company has not stated if the images were AI-generated, photos, or contained identifiable people. The company also revealed Friday that its models had attempted to hack the Department of Education’s website, and pulled data from the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The revelations are part of an ongoing review by OpenAI into the behavior of its models. As it dug into its records, following the Hugging Face hack, it’s uncovered more and more instances of “unexpected or concerning behavior.” It’s evidence not just of how difficult AI agents are becoming to control as they grow more advanced, but also of the challenge of tracking their actions. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they’re smart enough to try and cover their tracks. This has led to growing calls from researchers, those within the industry, and even some CEOs to call for slowing the pace of AI advancement.

body: Proaction ⁠ (opens in a new window) builds software for businesses that manage fleets of vehicles, from cars and trucks to construction machinery. Because every fleet operates differently, showing prospects how Proaction’s platform fits their business is an essential part of selling it.
But personalized demos required engineering time the team couldn’t spare. The founders had to rely on conversations and slide decks to explain what was possible. Codex flipped the script.

“As a non-technical person, I used to have to loop engineers in if I wanted a demo,” says Colin Knudsen, co-founder and COO of Proaction. “Now I do it myself in Codex.” Colin creates four to six customized, interactive demos a month, with each taking 30 to 45 minutes to build. He estimates that this avoids 40 to 60 hours of engineering work.

After a sales call, Colin directs Codex to the Granola recording, prospect email threads, and any spreadsheets the prospect has shared. Codex uses that context to customize an HTML demo environment that mirrors Proaction’s product and the customer’s own fleet.

highlights.title: Minecraft Confirms Ice Caves as Next Game Drop, Adds Frozen Zombies, Ice Balls, and More
highlights.summary: Mojang has teased Minecraft’s next game drop, giving fans a sneak peek at some of its features. As revealed at Minecraft LIVE, Ice Caves are coming to the game, adding a new and rare underground extension of cold biomes with glowing ice crystals and environmental variety.
body: Mojang said Ice Caves add a whole new layer of variety to cold biomes, making exploring underground even more interesting, thanks to the increased environmental diversity. “Though they may be beautiful, these caves are far from safe,” the developer said.

Ice crystals can be found in ice caves and can be placed both vertically and horizontally, providing lots of potential for decoration and building. They can even be used as a light source. The Frozen Zombie, meanwhile, applies a stacking freezing effect with its melee attacks. If you take enough hits, you'll freeze. It also throws ice balls at you, which apply knockback and deal damage. Normal zombies can convert into Frozen when exposed to powder snow. Players can already convert Husks into Zombies, and now Zombies into Frozen, opening the door for advanced mob farms.

Frozen drop ice balls on death, allowing players to use them as well, but they can also be crafted and used to brew a new potion. As a weapon, ice balls deal damage and apply knockback, and as a potion it can freeze players.

highlights.title: Minecraft Is Getting Its First New Dimension Since 2011
highlights.summary: In the wake of layoffs and studio reshuffling at Xbox earlier this week, Mojang held a Minecraft Live showcase to make several Minecraft -related announcements. While we didn't get a look at the next movie, Mojang revealed a game-changing addition to Minecraft.
body: Mojang gave us a first look at the Sift at Minecraft Live and confirmed it will be added to Minecraft Java Edition and Minecraft Bedrock Edition in 2027. Before then, the Sift will play an important role in Minecraft Dungeons 2, a Diablo-like action-RPG spin-off set to launch on Sept. 29. From Minecraft Dungeons 2 's segment of Minecraft Live, we can tell the Sift is an ethereal, spirit-world-like dimension.

Currently, Minecraft consists of three fairly ubiquitous dimensions: the Overworld, the Nether, and the End. By the time the game exited its public alpha and beta testing in Nov. 2011, all three of those dimensions were part of the game. In the nearly 15 years since, Mojang has simply expanded the content available in those dimensions rather than adding any new ones. That'll finally change next year.

While that's certainly the highest-profile announcement from this Minecraft Live, the reveals didn't stop there. Mojang showed how the next game drop will add ice caves as a new underground biome. In ice caves, players can fight the new Frozen Zombie mob, equip and craft the ice balls those enemies fight with, and mine ice crystals.

highlights.title: Apple Slab Pie
highlights.summary: There’s almost nothing that signals fall to me like the smell of an apple pie baking in my kitchen. And when that’s happening there’s a high likelihood I’ll be gathering with friends and family in the near future because, well, pies are meant to be shared!While I love a traditional lattice-topped…
body: I’ve spent more than a decade developing and styling recipes for all things sweet, starting in the Martha Stewart Living test kitchen, where meticulously perfected pies were in constant rotation no matter the time of year. I’m a big believer in approachable desserts that deliver maximum impact with minimal fuss, and this sizable pie checks all the right boxes. It feels special enough for a holiday, but still simple enough for a casual gathering.
Dice 4 1/2 sticks cold unsalted butter. Divide into 4 portions (4 1/2 ounces each), and refrigerate until ready to use.
Pulse 2 3/4 cups of the all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 teaspoons of the granulated sugar, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt together in a food processor a few times to combine.
Scatter 1 portion of the butter cubes over the flour. Pulse until the butter is cut into pieces no larger than a pea, about 10 (1-second) pulses.

highlights.title: Can Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince save the web from AI?
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Matthew Prince, who is CEO of Cloudflare. This episode is part of a two-part series on the future of business. Matthew last joined us on the show about two and a half years ago, at what we thought then was a wild pivot point for the internet — and now it
body: Cloudflare found in June that bots made up more than half of internet traffic. That number just keeps going up as more and more AI companies scrape more and more of the web, and now as more and more AI agents try and do things for people on the web. Cloudflare sits between websites and all those agents, and allows website owners some level of control: Owners can block all those AI tools, allow them, or, as you’ll hear, only allow those that might pay money for access.

So Matthew and I talked about how to control all these bots, what kind of mess they’re making of the web, and what kinds of information might be valuable in the future as some of the payment schemes come into focus. You’ll hear me ask pretty directly if some of the outcomes he’s describing are actually good — Matthew is a thoughtful guy, and his answer is something I’m still thinking about well after we had this conversation.

highlights.title: Appeals Court Lets the Pentagon Designate Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk
highlights.summary: The AI lab had argued multiple violations of its rights, but a divided panel of judges sided with the Trump administration.
body: Anthropic lost a legal battle to overturn one of the supply-chain risk labels that the US Department of Defense slapped on the company, as a federal appeals court in DC on Friday refused to second-guess the Trump administration.

“The department had ample support for its conclusion that the continued integration of Claude into the department’s information systems, by the department or its contractors, presented a statutorily covered national-security risk,” the judges wrote in a majority opinion. “As Anthropic admits, the company encodes restrictions into Claude that prevent the model from performing tasks that Anthropic wishes to prevent.”

Anthropic spokesperson Danielle Cohen says the company remains confident in its position and is considering all options. That could include appealing to a broader panel of the DC Circuit Court of Appeals or the US Supreme Court.

highlights.title: The Most Delicious Beef Stew of All Time
highlights.summary: Editor’s Note: If you’ve cooked this beloved recipe before, it might look a little different these days! We recently improved it to make it even easier to follow and more delicious.There are few meals more comforting than a big pot of something slowly simmering away on the stove — especially when…
body: A rich, comforting beef stew with tender chunks of beef, hearty vegetables, fresh herbs, and a deeply savory, flavorful gravy.

The potatoes and carrots go in toward the end so they become perfectly tender without turning mushy, and a handful of peas adds a pop of sweetness and color. Best of all, once everything is simmering, the heat does most of the work for you. Serve this stew straight from the pot with plenty of crusty bread or on a bed of mashed potatoes with a sprinkling of fresh chopped parsley. It is the coziest, most satisfying dinner that makes the long simmer completely worth the wait.

After attending two culinary schools, I’ve spent more than a decade working behind the scenes in test kitchens and on some of America’s favorite cooking shows. I love developing approachable recipes that are easy enough for a weeknight but still feel special and deliver big flavor without making cooking feel like rocket science.
This beef stew can be made up to 1 day in advance. Let cool, then cover and refrigerate. Reheat over medium heat, stirring occasionally until warmed through.
